38|     `{"step":"write"|"build"|"measure"|"fix"|"done"|"error", "round":1..3, "detail":str, ...}`.

45|     matches your numbers"), and a small note "self-check, not the exam referee";
46|     `BUILT` → neutral badge "Built (size not checked)" with the reason;
47|     `CHECK FAILED` → neutral badge "Checks failed: see measurements". Never show PASS for anything else. Show the measurements as small chips, the code in a collapsible `<pre>`,
48|     and STL/STEP/code download links. Show a 3D view of the STL with three.js r160 from a pinned CDN URL
49|     (OrbitControls, steel material, slow auto-rotate, teal edges). If WebGL fails, hide the viewer.
50|   - `error` (HTTP 429/413/5xx or an error event): show the message from the server in the panel, never a stack trace.
51|4. Input: limit the textarea to 600 characters with a visible counter. The 3 example chips fill in full example jobs
52|   (write 3 realistic CadQuery jobs: L-bracket with 2 holes, flanged pipe adapter, electronics box with lid lip, each
53|   with all dimensions in mm).

60|   dark corner tabs on mobile).
61|

63|- index.html, styles.css, app.js, object.jpeg and recorded_run.json exist; recorded_run.json parses, every event has a

70|browser without any model.
71|
72|---
73|
74|## Round P2: the backend (Modal web app)
75|
76|Create `deploy/modal_web.py` (Modal app name `homegrown-web`, CPU only, `min_containers=0`) and
77|`app/backend/` (pure-Python logic, importable and testable without Modal):
78|
79|- **Serving:** a FastAPI ASGI app that serves `app/web/` at `/`, plus:
80|  - `GET /api/status`: `paused` if the daily budget is used up; otherwise `ready` if a cheap probe of the model
81|    endpoint (`GET {FORGE_URL}/v1/models`, 3 s timeout) answers, else `waking` (and fire one non-blocking warm-up
82|    request).
83|  - `POST /api/build`: SSE stream as in P1.
84|  - `POST /api/lead`: append `{"tool","email","ts"}` to a Modal Dict `homegrown-leads` (email ≤ 200 chars, tool ≤
85|    300 chars; reject otherwise). Never log emails to stdout.
86|  - `GET /files/<run_id>.(stl|step|py)`: files kept in a Modal Dict `homegrown-files` for 24 h.
87|- **The loop (same as the 92% second look, FTX):** the model is the trained Glimmer served by
88|  `deploy/modal_forge.py` (served name `forge`; URL from env `FORGE_URL`; key from the existing Modal secret
89|  `forge-glimmer`, env `VLLM_API_KEY`). Messages start from `runner_final.ft_messages(job)`. Then up to 3 model calls:
90|  after a crash append the assistant reply and `runner.bx_error_message(error)`; after a build append
91|  `runner.bx_self_check_message(measure)`; a reply without a code fence ("DONE") ends the loop. Build every request body exactly as the FTX arm does (`runner.build_bx_body`: 16,000 max tokens, the same
92|  temperature/top_p/top_k, and the same reasoning setting). Make the reasoning strength ONE setting, env `REASONING_STRENGTH`
93|  (allowed: "high" or "xhigh"; default "xhigh" = what the 92% second look used, verifier F1). The decision is open: the user
94|  asked whether "high" (what the model was trained on) is better or faster; a small check on factory practice jobs decides
95|  before deploy. Test: the body sent to the model carries exactly the configured value. Import these helpers (`runner` is experiments/first-test/runner.py, imported by runner_final.py the same way); do not copy-paste them. If an import is impossible
96|  without side effects, stop and report it instead of rewriting them.
97|- **The box:** each answer runs in `cloud_cq.run_answer_in_box(code)` (the locked Modal sandbox, app `forge-cq`).
98|  Measurements come from its measure output. The **verdict on the page is a no-reference self-check**, because a
99|  visitor's job has no reference part: Three verdicts (verifier S1):
100|  `PASS` only if the part built, `solids == 1`, AND the job states an overall size that matches the bounding-box
101|  extents within 0.5% per axis; `BUILT` if it built with 1 solid but no overall size could be parsed (reason "size not
102|  checked"); `CHECK FAILED` otherwise, with reasons. "Overall size" is parsed ONLY from explicit patterns, written as a
103|  documented list of regexes, e.g. "overall (size|dimensions) A × B × C mm", "A x B x C mm box/plate/block",
104|  "base A × B × C mm" (+ "wall … N mm tall" adding height only when the job says so). Compare sorted extents to
105|  sorted stated numbers (axis order is not guaranteed). When unsure, return BUILT, never PASS. The function is `app/backend/selfcheck.py:self_check(job_text, measurements) -> (verdict, reasons)`.
106|  Keep it simple and conservative, and test it.
107|- **Files:** convert the built BREP to STL (tolerance 0.1 mm) and STEP inside the CPU web container (CadQuery 2.8.0,
108|  same pins as `cloud_cq.pip_spec()`). Never execute visitor-supplied or model code in the web container: only the
109|  sandbox runs code. The web container only reads the BREP that the sandbox returns.
110|- **Protection (all limits in one config block at the top of modal_web.py, read from env with these defaults):**
111|  - `MAX_JOB_CHARS=600` → 413.
112|  - Per IP: `MAX_BUILDS_PER_IP_HOUR=4` → 429 with "Please wait a bit…".
113|  - Global: `MAX_CONCURRENT_BUILDS=2` → 429 "Busy, try again in a minute".
114|  - (verifier S3) The web function runs with `max_containers=1`, and counters/limits live in that one process behind an
115|    asyncio lock (Modal Dict has no atomic counter; the Dict is only for persistence across restarts). The client IP
116|    comes from the connection peer / the LAST hop added by Modal's proxy, never the first X-Forwarded-For entry. Run
117|    ids are `uuid4().hex`.
118|  - **Daily budget:** `DAILY_CAP_USD=20` (the user's number; Claude may change it at deploy). Cost estimate per build
119|    = model GPU seconds × `GPU_USD_PER_S=0.000694` (A100-80GB ≈ $2.50/h) + `SANDBOX_USD_PER_BUILD=0.002`, plus
120|    (verifier S4) the idle tail after the last build of a burst: `IDLE_TAIL_USD=0.21` (300 s scale-down) charged once
121|    per burst, and `WAKE_USD=0.45` charged each time a warm-up is actually fired. Warm-ups are throttled: at most one per
122|    10 minutes globally and one per hour per IP; `/api/status` otherwise only reports the state and never wakes the
123|    model. The spend is kept in a Modal Dict keyed by
124|    UTC date. At or over the cap, `/api/status` returns `paused` and `/api/build` returns 429 with the paused message.
125|  - (verifier S5) A whole build has a `BUILD_LIMIT_S=600` wall-clock limit → error event "This part took too long;
126|    try a simpler one". Send the first SSE event immediately and a heartbeat comment at least every 15 s. The web
127|    function timeout is larger than the limit (≥ 660 s).
128|  - Model output and errors shown to visitors are capped at 4,000 characters and HTML-escaped by the page.
129|- **What goes into the web image (verifier S2):** an explicit file list only: `app/web/*`, `app/backend/*`,
130|  `experiments/final/runner_final.py`, `experiments/final/cloud_cq.py`, `experiments/final/run_cq_box.py`,
131|  `experiments/first-test/runner.py` and the minimum they import (list each file). Never `experiments/first-test/
132|  expected.json`, `jobs.py`, any `results/` or exam file. Use only `cloud_cq.run_answer_in_box`; do not use or deploy
133|  the grader app. Test: build the file list and assert the forbidden files are absent.
134|- No Claude, no other model, no analytics, no third-party calls except the three.js CDN in the page.
135|
136|Tests (`app/tests/`, pytest, all with fakes; no Modal, no network):
137|- the loop with a fake model + fake box: crash → fix → build → PASS gives event order write, build, fix, write, build,
138|  measure, done; messages match the FTX rules exactly (round 1 == ft_messages(job)); max 3 model calls;
139|- `self_check`: correct box → PASS; 2 solids → CHECK FAILED; wrong extent → CHECK FAILED; a job with no stated
140|  overall size → BUILT ("size not checked"), never PASS; ambiguous text → BUILT; each regex pattern has a test;
141|- limits: 601 chars → 413; 5th build from one IP in an hour → 429; a third concurrent build → 429; spend at the cap
142|  → status paused and build 429; the wake charge is added once per cold probe;
143|- the cost model: one build in a burst charges GPU seconds + sandbox + one idle tail; a fired warm-up charges WAKE_USD;
144|  a second warm-up within 10 min is not fired; status calls never wake the model by themselves;
145|- the IP used for limits ignores a spoofed first X-Forwarded-For hop; run ids are 32-hex uuid4;
146|- the SSE stream sends its first event before the first model call and a heartbeat during a slow fake model;
147|- `/api/lead` rejects a 201-char email; the lead is not printed to stdout;
148|- no secret value in any HTML/JS/JSON under app/web (grep for VLLM_API_KEY's env name and "es_").
149|
150|## Report (each round)
151|Diff summary, the exact pytest command and result (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q app/tests` plus the existing
152|`experiments/final experiments/r5` suites, which must stay green), and anything you could not follow or decided
153|differently (with the reason).

1|"""Daily money budget and warm-up throttle (pure part of verifier S4).
2|
3|Cost per build = model GPU seconds x GPU_USD_PER_S + SANDBOX_USD_PER_BUILD,
4|plus the idle tail after the last build of a burst (IDLE_TAIL_USD, charged
5|once per burst: a build that starts a new burst -- no build in the last
6|BURST_GAP_S -- carries it) and WAKE_USD each time a warm-up is actually
7|fired. Warm-ups are throttled: at most one per 10 minutes globally and one
8|per hour per IP. Spend is kept keyed by UTC date; at or over the cap the
9|API reports paused and refuses builds.
10|
11|Tests drive this with a fake clock; ``deploy/modal_web.py`` mirrors the
12|numbers into a Modal Dict for persistence across restarts.
13|"""
14|
15|import datetime
16|import time
17|
18|from . import config
19|
20|
21|def day_key(now=None):
22|    """UTC date string for today's spend bucket."""
23|    t = time.time() if now is None else now
24|    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
25|        t, tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
26|
27|
28|class Budget:
29|    """Spend ledger + warm-up throttle (one web process)."""
30|
31|    def __init__(self, now=None):
32|        self._now = now or time.time
33|        self._spend = {}  # day_key -> dollars
34|        self._last_build = None  # unix seconds of the last charged build
35|        self._last_warmup = None  # unix seconds of the last fired warm-up
36|        self._ip_warmups = {}  # ip -> unix seconds of its last warm-up
37|
38|    # -- spend ---------------------------------------------------------
39|    def spent_today(self):
40|        """Dollars charged in the current UTC day."""
41|        return self._spend.get(day_key(self._now()), 0.0)
42|
43|    def is_capped(self):
44|        """True once today's spend is at or over the daily cap."""
45|        return self.spent_today() >= config.DAILY_CAP_USD
46|
47|    def _add(self, dollars):
48|        key = day_key(self._now())
49|        self._spend[key] = self._spend.get(key, 0.0) + dollars
50|        return dollars
51|
52|    def charge_build(self, gpu_seconds):
53|        """Charge one build; returns the dollars added.
54|
55|        GPU seconds plus one sandbox fee, plus one idle tail when this
56|        build starts a new burst.
57|        """
58|        t = self._now()
59|        try:
60|            gpu = float(gpu_seconds or 0.0)
61|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
62|            gpu = 0.0
63|        cost = gpu * config.GPU_USD_PER_S + config.SANDBOX_USD_PER_BUILD
64|        if self._last_build is None or \
65|                t - self._last_build > config.BURST_GAP_S:
66|            cost += config.IDLE_TAIL_USD  # one tail per burst
67|        self._last_build = t
68|        return self._add(cost)
69|
70|    # -- warm-ups ------------------------------------------------------
71|    def may_warmup(self, ip):
72|        """True when a warm-up for this IP may fire now (throttled)."""
73|        t = self._now()
74|        if self._last_warmup is not None and \
75|                t - self._last_warmup < config.WARMUP_GLOBAL_S:
76|            return False
77|        last = self._ip_warmups.get(ip)
78|        if last is not None and t - last < config.WARMUP_IP_S:
79|            return False
80|        return True
81|
82|    def note_warmup(self, ip):
83|        """Record an actually-fired warm-up and charge WAKE_USD."""
84|        t = self._now()
85|        self._last_warmup = t
86|        self._ip_warmups[ip] = t
87|        return self._add(config.WAKE_USD)
88|
89|    # -- status --------------------------------------------------------
90|    def status(self, probe_ok):
91|        """(state, message) with NO side effects.
92|
93|        Never wakes the model by itself: when the state is "waking" the
94|        caller decides (via may_warmup/note_warmup) whether to actually
95|        fire a warm-up request.
96|        """
97|        if self.is_capped():
98|            return "paused", config.PAUSED_MESSAGE
99|        if probe_ok:
100|            return "ready", "The model is ready"
101|        return ("waking",
102|                "Waking up the model (this takes a few minutes). "
103|                "Here is a recorded run meanwhile.")

3|Messages start from ``runner_final.ft_messages(job)``. Then up to 3 model

6|are appended; a reply without a code fence ("DONE") ends the loop. Every
7|request body is built exactly as the FTX arm builds it
8|(``runner.build_bx_body``: 16,000 max tokens, same temperature/top_p/top_k
9|and the same reasoning setting), except the reasoning strength comes from
10|the ONE ``REASONING_STRENGTH`` setting (env, "high"|"xhigh", default
11|"xhigh"). With the default the body is byte-identical to
12|``runner.build_bx_body``.
13|
14|``model_call(messages, body)`` returns ``(content, gpu_seconds)``.
15|``box_run(code)`` returns a ``cloud_cq.run_answer_in_box``-style dict
16|``{"brep_bytes", "measure", "run_error"}``. Both are faked in tests; no
17|Modal, no network here.
18|"""

83|def run_job(job_text, model_call, box_run, model=MODEL_NAME,
84|            clock=None):
85|    """Yield SSE-style event dicts for one visitor job.
86|
87|    Event steps: write, build, fix, measure, done (or error). The first
88|    event is yielded before the first model call. The final done event
89|    carries verdict/reasons/measurements/code/rounds/seconds/gpu_seconds;

140|        yield {"step": "build", "round": rounds,
141|               "detail": "Building in the locked box."}
142|        best_code = code
143|        best_raw = measure_raw
144|        last_error = None
145|        if measure is None:
146|            break
147|        yield {"step": "measure", "round": rounds,
148|               "detail": _measure_line(measure),
149|               "measurements": measure_raw}
150|        # FTX rule (Claude fix 2026-11-02, disclosed): after a build the
151|        # model sees its own measurements and either fixes the part or says
152|        # DONE (no code fence), up to MAX_CALLS. The last built part counts.

154|                         "content": runner.bx_self_check_message(measure)})
155|        if rounds < MAX_CALLS:

157|                   "detail": "Checking its own measurements."}
158|    seconds = now() - t0
159|    if best_code:

161|    else:

163|                            [last_error or "the part did not build"])
164|    yield {"step": "done", "round": rounds, "verdict": verdict,
165|           "reason": "; ".join(reasons),
166|           "measurements": best_raw, "code": best_code,
167|           "rounds": rounds, "seconds": round(seconds, 3),

1|"""Daily money budget and warm-up throttle (pure part of verifier S4).
2|
3|Cost per build = model GPU seconds x GPU_USD_PER_S + SANDBOX_USD_PER_BUILD,
4|plus the idle tail after the last build of a burst (IDLE_TAIL_USD, charged
5|once per burst: a build that starts a new burst -- no build in the last
6|BURST_GAP_S -- carries it) and WAKE_USD each time a warm-up is actually
7|fired. Warm-ups are throttled: at most one per 10 minutes globally and one
8|per hour per IP. Spend is kept keyed by UTC date; at or over the cap the
9|API reports paused and refuses builds.
10|
11|Tests drive this with a fake clock; ``deploy/modal_web.py`` mirrors the
12|numbers into a Modal Dict for persistence across restarts.
13|"""
14|
15|import datetime
16|import time
17|
18|from . import config
19|
20|
21|def day_key(now=None):
22|    """UTC date string for today's spend bucket."""
23|    t = time.time() if now is None else now
24|    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
25|        t, tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
26|
27|
28|class Budget:
29|    """Spend ledger + warm-up throttle (one web process)."""
30|
31|    def __init__(self, now=None):
32|        self._now = now or time.time
33|        self._spend = {}  # day_key -> dollars
34|        self._last_build = None  # unix seconds of the last charged build
35|        self._last_warmup = None  # unix seconds of the last fired warm-up
36|        self._ip_warmups = {}  # ip -> unix seconds of its last warm-up
37|
38|    # -- spend ---------------------------------------------------------
39|    def spent_today(self):
40|        """Dollars charged in the current UTC day."""
41|        return self._spend.get(day_key(self._now()), 0.0)
42|
43|    def is_capped(self):
44|        """True once today's spend is at or over the daily cap."""
45|        return self.spent_today() >= config.DAILY_CAP_USD
46|
47|    def _add(self, dollars):
48|        key = day_key(self._now())
49|        self._spend[key] = self._spend.get(key, 0.0) + dollars
50|        return dollars
51|
52|    def charge_build(self, gpu_seconds):
53|        """Charge one build; returns the dollars added.
54|
55|        GPU seconds plus one sandbox fee, plus one idle tail when this
56|        build starts a new burst.
57|        """
58|        t = self._now()
59|        try:
60|            gpu = float(gpu_seconds or 0.0)
61|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
62|            gpu = 0.0
63|        cost = gpu * config.GPU_USD_PER_S + config.SANDBOX_USD_PER_BUILD
64|        if self._last_build is None or \
65|                t - self._last_build > config.BURST_GAP_S:
66|            cost += config.IDLE_TAIL_USD  # one tail per burst
67|        self._last_build = t
68|        return self._add(cost)
69|
70|    # -- warm-ups ------------------------------------------------------
71|    def may_warmup(self, ip):
72|        """True when a warm-up for this IP may fire now (throttled)."""
73|        t = self._now()
74|        if self._last_warmup is not None and \
75|                t - self._last_warmup < config.WARMUP_GLOBAL_S:
76|            return False
77|        last = self._ip_warmups.get(ip)
78|        if last is not None and t - last < config.WARMUP_IP_S:
79|            return False
80|        return True
81|
82|    def note_warmup(self, ip):
83|        """Record an actually-fired warm-up and charge WAKE_USD."""
84|        t = self._now()
85|        self._last_warmup = t
86|        self._ip_warmups[ip] = t
87|        return self._add(config.WAKE_USD)
88|
89|    # -- status --------------------------------------------------------
90|    def status(self, probe_ok):
91|        """(state, message) with NO side effects.
92|
93|        Never wakes the model by itself: when the state is "waking" the
94|        caller decides (via may_warmup/note_warmup) whether to actually
95|        fire a warm-up request.
96|        """
97|        if self.is_capped():
98|            return "paused", config.PAUSED_MESSAGE
99|        if probe_ok:
100|            return "ready", "The model is ready"
101|        return ("waking",
102|                "Waking up the model (this takes a few minutes). "

1|"""The 92%-second-look loop (FTX rules) with an injected model and box.
2|
3|Messages start from ``runner_final.ft_messages(job)``. Then up to 3 model
4|calls: after a crash the assistant reply plus ``runner.bx_error_message``
5|are appended; after a build the reply plus ``runner.bx_self_check_message``
6|are appended; a reply without a code fence ("DONE") ends the loop. Every
7|request body is built exactly as the FTX arm builds it
8|(``runner.build_bx_body``: 16,000 max tokens, same temperature/top_p/top_k
9|and the same reasoning setting), except the reasoning strength comes from
10|the ONE ``REASONING_STRENGTH`` setting (env, "high"|"xhigh", default
11|"xhigh"). With the default the body is byte-identical to
12|``runner.build_bx_body``.
13|
14|``model_call(messages, body)`` returns ``(content, gpu_seconds)``.
15|``box_run(code)`` returns a ``cloud_cq.run_answer_in_box``-style dict
16|``{"brep_bytes", "measure", "run_error"}``. Both are faked in tests; no
17|Modal, no network here.
18|"""
19|

1|"""Server-Sent Events helpers (verifier S5).
2|
3|The first data event goes out immediately and a ": heartbeat" comment goes
4|out at least every HEARTBEAT_S seconds so proxies do not cut the stream.
5|``deploy/modal_web.py`` drives ``with_heartbeat`` from asyncio; the pump
6|task means a slow model never blocks the heartbeat.
7|"""
8|
9|import asyncio
10|import json
11|
12|from . import config
13|
14|HEARTBEAT_LINE = ": heartbeat"
15|
16|
17|def encode_event(payload):
18|    """One SSE data frame for a JSON event dict."""
19|    return "data: %s\n\n" % json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"))
20|
21|
22|def encode_heartbeat():
23|    """One SSE comment frame (keeps the stream alive)."""
24|    return "%s\n\n" % HEARTBEAT_LINE
25|
26|
27|def error_event(detail):
28|    """An SSE event payload for a failed build."""
29|    text = str(detail or "Something went wrong building that part.")
30|    return {"step": "error", "detail": text[:config.OUTPUT_CAP]}
31|
32|
33|async def with_heartbeat(aiter, interval=None):
34|    """Yield SSE strings for an async event iterator, injecting heartbeats.
35|
36|    Events are pulled by a background task into a queue, so waiting for
37|    the next event never cancels the producer: whenever `interval`
38|    seconds pass without an event, a heartbeat comment is yielded.
39|    """
40|    gap = config.HEARTBEAT_S if interval is None else interval
41|    queue = asyncio.Queue()
42|    finished = object()
43|
44|    async def _pump():
45|        try:
46|            async for event in aiter:
47|                await queue.put(event)
48|        finally:
49|            await queue.put(finished)
50|
51|    task = asyncio.ensure_future(_pump())
52|    try:
53|        while True:
54|            try:
55|                item = await asyncio.wait_for(queue.get(), timeout=gap)
56|            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
57|                yield encode_heartbeat()
58|                continue
59|            if item is finished:
60|                return
61|            yield encode_event(item)
62|    finally:
63|        if not task.done():
64|            task.cancel()

1|"""No-reference self-check for a visitor's job (verifier S1).
2|
3|A visitor's job has no reference part, so the page verdict is conservative:
4|PASS only when the part built with exactly 1 solid AND the job states an
5|overall size (parsed ONLY by the patterns below) matching the measured
6|bounding-box extents within 0.5% per axis. BUILT when it built with 1 solid
7|but no overall size could be parsed ("size not checked"). CHECK FAILED
8|otherwise. When unsure, return BUILT, never PASS.
9|
10|Overall size is parsed ONLY from these explicit patterns (axis order is not
11|guaranteed, so sorted extents are compared to sorted stated numbers):
12|
13|1. OVERALL:  "overall size|dimensions A x B x C mm"
14|2. BOXNOUN:  "A x B x C mm box|plate|block"
15|3. BASE_WALL: "base A x B x C mm" plus "wall ... N mm tall" elsewhere in the
16|   job; the wall sits on the base, so the stated size is A x B x (C + N).
17|   ("adding height only when the job says so": without the wall phrase a
18|   bare "base ..." is NOT an overall size.)
19|
20|"x" stands for any of: x X * xU+00D7 or the word "by"; numbers may be
21|decimal; matching is case-insensitive.
22|"""
23|
24|import re
25|
26|TOL = 0.005  # 0.5% per axis
27|
28|_NUM = r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)"
29|_SEP = "(?:\u00d7|x|X|\\*|by)"  # \u00d7 is the multiplication sign
30|_TRIPLE = _NUM + r"\s*" + _SEP + r"\s*" + _NUM + r"\s*" + _SEP + r"\s*" + _NUM
31|
32|PATTERNS = (
33|    ("OVERALL",
34|     re.compile(r"overall\s+(?:size|dimensions?)\s*(?:is|:)?\s*"
35|                + _TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
36|    ("BOXNOUN",
37|     re.compile(_TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\s*(?:box|plate|block)\b",
38|                re.IGNORECASE)),
39|    ("BASE",
40|     re.compile(r"base\s+" + _TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
41|)
42|WALL_TALL_RE = re.compile(r"wall[^.\n]{0,80}?" + _NUM + r"\s*mm\s*tall\b",
43|                           re.IGNORECASE)
44|
45|
46|def pattern_names():
47|    """Names of the documented overall-size patterns."""
48|    return [name for name, _ in PATTERNS] + ["BASE_WALL"]
49|
50|
51|def parse_overall_size(job_text):
52|    """(pattern_name, (a, b, c)) or (None, None) when nothing parsed.
53|
54|    BASE_WALL only matches when the job ALSO states the wall height; a
55|    bare "base ..." yields (None, None).
56|    """
57|    text = job_text or ""
58|    for name, rx in PATTERNS:
59|        m = rx.search(text)
60|        if not m:
61|            continue
62|        if name == "BASE":
63|            w = WALL_TALL_RE.search(text)
64|            if not w:
65|                continue  # a bare base is not an overall size
66|            try:
67|                dims = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)),
68|                        float(m.group(3)) + float(w.group(1)))
69|            except (TypeError, ValueError):
70|                continue
71|            return "BASE_WALL", dims
72|        try:
73|            dims = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)),
74|                    float(m.group(3)))
75|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
76|            continue
77|        return name, dims
78|    return None, None
79|
80|
81|def measure_extents(measurements):
82|    """[x, y, z] extents from a box or recorded measurement dict, or None."""
83|    if not isinstance(measurements, dict):
84|        return None
85|    for key in ("bbox_mm", "extents_mm"):
86|        vals = measurements.get(key)
87|        if isinstance(vals, (list, tuple)) and len(vals) == 3:
88|            try:
89|                return [float(v) for v in vals]
90|            except (TypeError, ValueError):
91|                return None
92|    bbox = measurements.get("bbox")
93|    if isinstance(bbox, (list, tuple)) and len(bbox) == 6:
94|        try:
95|            lo = [float(bbox[0]), float(bbox[1]), float(bbox[2])]
96|            hi = [float(bbox[3]), float(bbox[4]), float(bbox[5])]
97|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
98|            return None
99|        return [hi[i] - lo[i] for i in range(3)]
100|    return None
101|
102|
103|def _fmt(dims):
104|    return " \u00d7 ".join(
105|        ("%g" % v) for v in dims) + " mm"
106|
107|
108|def self_check(job_text, measurements):
109|    """(verdict, reasons). Verdict is PASS, BUILT or CHECK FAILED."""
110|    if not isinstance(measurements, dict) or not measurements:
111|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["the part did not build"]
112|    try:
113|        solids = measurements.get("solids")
114|        n_solids = None if solids is None else int(solids)
115|    except (TypeError, ValueError):
116|        n_solids = None
117|    if n_solids is None:
118|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["could not count the solids"]
119|    if n_solids != 1:
120|        return ("CHECK FAILED",
121|                ["built %d solids, expected 1" % (n_solids,)])
122|    extents = measure_extents(measurements)
123|    if extents is None:
124|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["no size measurements"]
125|    _name, stated = parse_overall_size(job_text)
126|    if stated is None:
127|        return "BUILT", ["size not checked: no overall size stated"]
128|    lo = sorted(extents)
129|    hi = sorted(stated)
130|    for m, s in zip(lo, hi):
131|        if s == 0:
132|            ok = (m == 0)
133|        else:
134|            ok = abs(m - s) <= TOL * abs(s) + 1e-9  # float hygiene
135|        if not ok:
136|            return ("CHECK FAILED",
137|                    ["overall size %s does not match measured %s"
138|                     % (_fmt(hi), _fmt(lo))])
139|    return ("PASS",
140|            ["built", "1 solid",
141|             "%s matches your numbers" % (_fmt(hi),)])

1|"""Server-Sent Events helpers (verifier S5).
2|
3|The first data event goes out immediately and a ": heartbeat" comment goes
4|out at least every HEARTBEAT_S seconds so proxies do not cut the stream.
5|``deploy/modal_web.py`` drives ``with_heartbeat`` from asyncio; the pump
6|task means a slow model never blocks the heartbeat.
7|"""
8|
9|import asyncio
10|import json
11|
12|from . import config
13|
14|HEARTBEAT_LINE = ": heartbeat"
15|
16|
17|def encode_event(payload):
18|    """One SSE data frame for a JSON event dict."""
19|    return "data: %s\n\n" % json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"))
20|
21|
22|def encode_heartbeat():
23|    """One SSE comment frame (keeps the stream alive)."""
24|    return "%s\n\n" % HEARTBEAT_LINE
25|
26|
27|def error_event(detail):
28|    """An SSE event payload for a failed build."""
29|    text = str(detail or "Something went wrong building that part.")
30|    return {"step": "error", "detail": text[:config.OUTPUT_CAP]}
31|
32|
33|async def with_heartbeat(aiter, interval=None):
34|    """Yield SSE strings for an async event iterator, injecting heartbeats.
35|
36|    Events are pulled by a background task into a queue, so waiting for
37|    the next event never cancels the producer: whenever `interval`
38|    seconds pass without an event, a heartbeat comment is yielded.
39|    """
40|    gap = config.HEARTBEAT_S if interval is None else interval
41|    queue = asyncio.Queue()
42|    finished = object()
43|
44|    async def _pump():
45|        try:
46|            async for event in aiter:
47|                await queue.put(event)
48|        finally:
49|            await queue.put(finished)
50|
51|    task = asyncio.ensure_future(_pump())
52|    try:
53|        while True:
54|            try:
55|                item = await asyncio.wait_for(queue.get(), timeout=gap)
56|            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
57|                yield encode_heartbeat()
58|                continue
59|            if item is finished:
60|                return
61|            yield encode_event(item)
62|    finally:
63|        if not task.done():
64|            task.cancel()

1|"""No-reference self-check for a visitor's job (verifier S1).
2|
3|A visitor's job has no reference part, so the page verdict is conservative:
4|PASS only when the part built with exactly 1 solid AND the job states an
5|overall size (parsed ONLY by the patterns below) matching the measured
6|bounding-box extents within 0.5% per axis. BUILT when it built with 1 solid
7|but no overall size could be parsed ("size not checked"). CHECK FAILED
8|otherwise. When unsure, return BUILT, never PASS.
9|
10|Overall size is parsed ONLY from these explicit patterns (axis order is not
11|guaranteed, so sorted extents are compared to sorted stated numbers):
12|
13|1. OVERALL:  "overall size|dimensions A x B x C mm"
14|2. BOXNOUN:  "A x B x C mm box|plate|block"
15|3. BASE_WALL: "base A x B x C mm" plus "wall ... N mm tall" elsewhere in the
16|   job; the wall sits on the base, so the stated size is A x B x (C + N).
17|   ("adding height only when the job says so": without the wall phrase a
18|   bare "base ..." is NOT an overall size.)
19|
20|"x" stands for any of: x X * xU+00D7 or the word "by"; numbers may be
21|decimal; matching is case-insensitive.
22|"""
23|
24|import re
25|
26|TOL = 0.005  # 0.5% per axis
27|
28|_NUM = r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)"
29|_SEP = "(?:\u00d7|x|X|\\*|by)"  # \u00d7 is the multiplication sign
30|_TRIPLE = _NUM + r"\s*" + _SEP + r"\s*" + _NUM + r"\s*" + _SEP + r"\s*" + _NUM
31|
32|PATTERNS = (
33|    ("OVERALL",
34|     re.compile(r"overall\s+(?:size|dimensions?)\s*(?:is|:)?\s*"
35|                + _TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
36|    ("BOXNOUN",
37|     re.compile(_TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\s*(?:box|plate|block)\b",
38|                re.IGNORECASE)),
39|    ("BASE",
40|     re.compile(r"base\s+" + _TRIPLE + r"\s*mm\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
41|)
42|WALL_TALL_RE = re.compile(r"wall[^.\n]{0,80}?" + _NUM + r"\s*mm\s*tall\b",
43|                           re.IGNORECASE)
44|
45|
46|def pattern_names():
47|    """Names of the documented overall-size patterns."""
48|    return [name for name, _ in PATTERNS] + ["BASE_WALL"]
49|
50|
51|def parse_overall_size(job_text):
52|    """(pattern_name, (a, b, c)) or (None, None) when nothing parsed.
53|
54|    BASE_WALL only matches when the job ALSO states the wall height; a
55|    bare "base ..." yields (None, None).
56|    """
57|    text = job_text or ""
58|    for name, rx in PATTERNS:
59|        m = rx.search(text)
60|        if not m:
61|            continue
62|        if name == "BASE":
63|            w = WALL_TALL_RE.search(text)
64|            if not w:
65|                continue  # a bare base is not an overall size
66|            try:
67|                dims = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)),
68|                        float(m.group(3)) + float(w.group(1)))
69|            except (TypeError, ValueError):
70|                continue
71|            return "BASE_WALL", dims
72|        try:
73|            dims = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)),
74|                    float(m.group(3)))
75|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
76|            continue
77|        return name, dims
78|    return None, None
79|
80|
81|def measure_extents(measurements):
82|    """[x, y, z] extents from a box or recorded measurement dict, or None."""
83|    if not isinstance(measurements, dict):
84|        return None
85|    for key in ("bbox_mm", "extents_mm"):
86|        vals = measurements.get(key)
87|        if isinstance(vals, (list, tuple)) and len(vals) == 3:
88|            try:
89|                return [float(v) for v in vals]
90|            except (TypeError, ValueError):
91|                return None
92|    bbox = measurements.get("bbox")
93|    if isinstance(bbox, (list, tuple)) and len(bbox) == 6:
94|        try:
95|            lo = [float(bbox[0]), float(bbox[1]), float(bbox[2])]
96|            hi = [float(bbox[3]), float(bbox[4]), float(bbox[5])]
97|        except (TypeError, ValueError):
98|            return None
99|        return [hi[i] - lo[i] for i in range(3)]
100|    return None
101|
102|
103|def _fmt(dims):
104|    return " \u00d7 ".join(
105|        ("%g" % v) for v in dims) + " mm"
106|
107|
108|def self_check(job_text, measurements):
109|    """(verdict, reasons). Verdict is PASS, BUILT or CHECK FAILED."""
110|    if not isinstance(measurements, dict) or not measurements:
111|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["the part did not build"]
112|    try:
113|        solids = measurements.get("solids")
114|        n_solids = None if solids is None else int(solids)
115|    except (TypeError, ValueError):
116|        n_solids = None
117|    if n_solids is None:
118|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["could not count the solids"]
119|    if n_solids != 1:
120|        return ("CHECK FAILED",
121|                ["built %d solids, expected 1" % (n_solids,)])
122|    extents = measure_extents(measurements)
123|    if extents is None:
124|        return "CHECK FAILED", ["no size measurements"]
125|    _name, stated = parse_overall_size(job_text)
126|    if stated is None:
127|        return "BUILT", ["size not checked: no overall size stated"]
128|    lo = sorted(extents)
129|    hi = sorted(stated)
130|    for m, s in zip(lo, hi):
131|        if s == 0:
132|            ok = (m == 0)
133|        else:
134|            ok = abs(m - s) <= TOL * abs(s) + 1e-9  # float hygiene
135|        if not ok:
136|            return ("CHECK FAILED",
137|                    ["overall size %s does not match measured %s"
138|                     % (_fmt(hi), _fmt(lo))])
139|    return ("PASS",
140|            ["built", "1 solid",
141|             "%s matches your numbers" % (_fmt(hi),)])

Round P2b is done. All four NO-GO findings are fixed and covered by tests.

## Diff summary

- [webapp.py](~/projects/forge/app/backend/webapp.py) (new): `make_app(deps)` factory building the real FastAPI app with model, box, convert, warmer, containers, leads/files stores, money/rates/lead-rates, wall/monotonic clocks, `build_limit_s`, `web_dir`, mirror/reconcile all injected. FastAPI is imported inside the factory so the module imports without it. Static mount stays LAST (Claude's W1 order fix kept).
- [modal_web.py](~/projects/forge/deploy/modal_web.py): now thin — `web()` builds real deps (model wrapper via `post_chat`, `cloud_cq` box, `convert_brep`, thread-spawning warmer, `_container_count()` via `get_current_stats` in try/except, Modal Dicts, spend mirror) and returns `make_app(deps)`. `probe_model` and its per-status `GET /v1/models` are gone; W2 warms only via throttled warm-up or real build.
- W2: [budget.py](~/projects/forge/app/backend/budget.py) gains `warm_until` (`note_model_response` sets last-response + 300 s), `is_warm()`, `note_cold_build()` (WAKE_USD once), and side-effect-free `warm_status()`; `status(probe_ok)` kept as a compat shim. `containers()>0` also counts as warm.
- W3: the build worker accumulates model seconds per finished call (returned value, measured latency on failure) and charges gpu + sandbox + idle-tail in one guarded `finally`, on done/timeout/exception/no-code/closed-tab (disconnect hits the same `finally` via generator close).
- W4: [loop.py](~/projects/forge/app/backend/loop.py) takes `deadline` and starts no new model call or box run past it; `_model_call` uses `timeout=min(600, deadline-now)`; one worker thread runs the whole loop and releases the slot in its own `finally`. `RateState`/`Budget` are lock-guarded for thread use.
- Small: `LeadRate` (5/hour → 429, in [limits.py](~/projects/forge/app/backend/limits.py), limit in [config.py](~/projects/forge/app/backend/config.py) as `MAX_LEADS_PER_IP_HOUR` plus `SCALE_DOWN_S`); lead `delete` (trimmed, case-insensitive) removes all same-email leads, stores nothing, returns `{"ok": true, "deleted": n}`; new privacy line in [index.html](~/projects/forge/app/web/index.html); [app.js](~/projects/forge/app/web/app.js) drops `CONTACT_EMAIL`/`mailto` and shows "Deleted."; `dev_server.py` out of the image list (file kept), plus an explicit 404 guard route so the served set is exactly the five page files.
- Tests: new [test_p2b_webapp.py](~/projects/forge/app/tests/test_p2b_webapp.py) (21 tests); [test_web_static.py](~/projects/forge/app/tests/test_web_static.py) and [test_p2_image.py](~/projects/forge/app/tests/test_p2_image.py) updated for the removed placeholder and new config keys.

## Test commands and results

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q app/tests` → **90 passed** (69 existing + 21 new).
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/r5` → **115 passed**, still green.

## Deviations and notes

- `Budget.status(probe_ok)` was kept (as a shim over `warm_status`) instead of removed, so the existing budget tests keep passing unchanged; the web layer only uses `warm_status()`.
- A cold build charges WAKE via `note_cold_build()` without touching the warm-up throttle timestamps; a status poll mid-boot can therefore fire one extra throttled warm-up (over-charging, i.e. the safe direction for the cap).
- Closed-tab charging is by construction (worker-thread `finally`, independent of the HTTP side) rather than a dedicated disconnect test — TestClient has no clean disconnect injection.
- Bug found by the new tests: the `/files` handler was named `files`, rebinding the closure holding the file store so nothing was ever stored; the store variable is now `file_store`.
- Untouched per rules: no network/Modal/model calls, no deploy, no pip install, no push; changes only under `app/` and `deploy/modal_web.py` (the untracked `results/muse-product-*` files are other sessions' artifacts, not mine).
